title: Automatic Escalation Policy for Request Throttling and Circuit Isolation
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Problem: During regional surges we observe correlated 429 spikes, request timeouts, and transient ERROR_RATE increases. Current fallback logic is mostly static thresholds which either trigger too early (unnecessary failovers) or too late (customer-visible errors). This ticket defines an adaptive escalation policy that combines short-term throttling signals (429 bursts), latency/timeouts, and error-rate momentum to drive circuit isolation and model-variant failovers per region and per-tenant. The goal is to reduce user impact while containing blast radius and preserving high-priority traffic.
proposal: Introduce a multi-signal escalation controller that computes a decaying ‘escalation score’ per (region, tier, tenant) and maps score ranges to actions: soft-throttle, route-shift to lower-cost variant, isolate tenant (circuit open), or global failover. Signals: 429 rate (burst detector), median p95 latency increase, consecutive request timeouts, and error-rate slope over 5m. The controller uses hysteresis windows and a cooldown decay profile per action. Actions are reversible and annotated in tracing for post-mortem analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Escalation score calculation validated in staging against synthetic surge scripts (scripts attached).
Automatic soft-throttle action reduces effective RPS to configured target without increasing 500-level errors by >1%.
Per-tenant circuit breaker prevents >95% of subsequent errors for isolated tenant during active isolation window.
Rollout shows <2% false-positive failovers in a 72-hour canary against production traffic slice.
Dashboard: real-time escalation score, action history, and per-tenant cooldown remaining available in Console.
design_considerations: Score composition must be explainable (weighted sum + time-decay) to allow SRE tuning.
Prefer soft actions (throttle/reroute) before hard actions (isolate) to reduce customer surprises.
Tenant isolation should be scoped and auditable; provide immediate manual override from Console.
Keep lightweight path for evaluation to avoid adding significant latency to routing decision (~<1ms extra).
Compatibility with Dedicated and Private deployments: configurable via policy YAML, reasonable defaults for hosted.
implementation_steps: 1) Implement signal collectors: 429 burst detector, timeout counter, latency p95 delta, error-rate slope (ENG-31802 reference for signal smoothing).
2) Build escalation-score service (stateless workers with Redis-backed short-term buckets) with configurable weights and decay constants.
3) Integrate decision API into smart-router so decisions can be executed: throttle tokens, route to model-variant, mark tenant-isolated.
4) Add tracing and event logs for each action with correlation IDs and reason codes.
5) Add Console widgets and alerting rules (see monitoring_and_alerting).
6) Canary rollout: 0.5% traffic -> 5% -> 20% with ops watch and automatic rollback triggers.
7) Post-canny 2-week burn to tune weights and decay constants based on false-positive/negative metrics.
rollout_strategy: Feature flag gated behind runtime-1.22; enable for internal tenants first.
Canary cohorts by region (US-EAST -> EU-WEST -> APAC) and by tenant risk profile.
Automatic rollback if error-rate increases by >3% or if customer-impacted latency >100ms for >10m.
monitoring_and_alerting: New Grafana panels: escalation_score (histogram), action_rate (throttle/reroute/isolate), false_positive_rate.
Pager alert if cascade of isolations >3 regions within 10m.
SLO alert: guardrail if global 5xx rate increases >1% post-rollout step.
Audit log stream to BigQuery for forensic queries and billing reconciliation.
Synthetic probes to validate that soft-throttle still returns valid model responses within latency SLO.
metrics: Primary: reduction in customer-visible 5xx and timeout rates during surge windows.
Secondary: number of tenant isolations, mean isolation duration, rollback occurrences.
Operational: decision API P99 latency, additional CPU/RAM per routing node.
Economic: token cost delta when routing to lower-cost variants during surges.
qa_steps: Run synthetic surge test harness (scripts in repo) and verify escalation_score trajectory matches expected patterns.
Validate manual override from Console suspends actions within 30s.
Confirm trace correlation and action logging in staging BigQuery exports.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: We favor explainability over opaque ML-driven classifiers for now to keep incident response simple. If this approach reduces false positives adequately, follow-up ticket will explore ML-based signal fusion. Also discussed exposing per-tenant policies for enterprise customers (configurable thresholds and cooldowns).
